metadata.rules_text:
- Overestimate after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.70 sentiment → forecast too high).
- Underestimate during strong negative sentiment; model fails to drop sharply when sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.50 → forecast stays high).
- Lag in correction: model often holds high forecasts for 2–3 days after sentiment shifts, especially after +0.70 sentiment.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; true price often reverts to 30–45 day moving average after spikes.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts overestimate early in the window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; underpredict later days when sentiment stabilizes.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.70 in last 3 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.50, increase forecast by 5–10% to account for downward pressure.
